replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics has always been my favorite subject. I find logic and problem-solving in it really satisfying. As a full-time student, I enjoy the challenge of working through complex problems. It’s something I can focus on deeply, which fits my conscientious nature. I don’t see it as intimidating, but rather as a tool for understanding the world.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Sometimes I feel stressed when I face unfamiliar or highly abstract topics. It’s not a constant feeling, but I do feel some pressure during exams or tight deadlines.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used AI last year to help clarify concepts. It was useful for checking my work and getting step-by-step explanations. replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, identify the equation in the form ax² + bx + c = 0. Next, calculate the discriminant, b² - 4ac, to see the nature of the roots. Then, use the quadratic formula: x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of the discriminant, all divided by 2a. Finally, simplify the result to find the solutions.

Start by finding the first derivative of the function, dy/dx. Set this derivative equal to zero to find critical points. Solve for x. Then, substitute these x-values back into the original function to get the y-coordinates. Finally, use the second derivative test to determine if each point is a maximum, minimum, or saddle point.
